scenarios.title: Store a credential, edit it, use it
scenarios.say: A person stores a credential in their own vault, edits its notes without re-entering the secret, and the gateway uses it at request time. The backend logs who actually acted; with a shared service account it logs the same identity for everyone.

steps.say: maya.chen stores a bearer token for ledger-api (a mock credential the lab generates).
The notes are edited. The secret is omitted, so the stored value is kept untouched.
The agent asks ledger-api for a summary. The gateway injects maya.chen's own credential; the agent never sees it.
The same call through a shared service account, for contrast.
omar.reyes makes the same shared-account call: the backend logs the same identity.

scenarios.title: Delete, restore, then purge after 24 hours
scenarios.say: A deletion is staged, not immediate. It can be restored inside the window, and it is purged at exactly 24 hours: one minute short and it is still there.

steps.say: maya.chen stores a credential for ledger-api.
The entry is deleted: staged, with a purge time 24 hours away.
Changed their mind: restored, nothing lost.
Deleted again.
The lab clock moves 23 hours 59 minutes. The entry is still staged.
A staged entry cannot be used.
One more minute: exactly 24 hours. The entry is purged.
Restoring is now impossible: it is gone.

The administrator names the owner in the call. There is no such parameter: the call is refused.

An API key for the cards system.
A user name and password for reports, sent as HTTP Basic.
A pair of custom headers for the partner gateway.
Call 1: bearer.
Call 2: API key.
Call 3: Basic.
Call 4: custom headers.

scenarios.title: Create, rotate, soft-delete and purge in a secret store
scenarios.say: In Azure Key Vault a secret gets created, rotated, soft-deleted, recovered, soft-deleted again and purged. Soft-delete and purge exist only where the deck lists them (Azure): AWS refuses. A Delinea secret with a file field is created too.

steps.say: maya.chen creates a secret in kv-payments-prod (the lab generates a mock value).
Rotate it on demand: a new version, a rotation counter.
Delete: Azure soft-deletes, so it is recoverable.
Recover it.
Delete again.
Purge: gone for good.
On AWS the same user only holds read, so a delete is refused.
The administrator holds write on AWS, but AWS has no soft-delete here: refused.
A Delinea secret from the Secure-File template, with a file field.

scenarios.title: Read and write are separate grants
scenarios.say: The user can read an AWS secret but not rotate it; the administrator can rotate it but not read it. A value is delivered only to a simulated consumer, never into an API response. Everything is audited, allowed or denied.

steps.say: maya.chen reads the AWS database secret: the value goes to the simulated gateway, masked here.
maya.chen tries to rotate it: read is granted, write is not.
sam.jones tries to read it: write is granted, read is not.
The administrator rotates it: allowed.
ana.silva has no grant at all: the secret is not found.
The administrator grants ana.silva read on the AWS payments secrets.
Now the read is allowed, and delivered to the consumer.

scenarios.title: The nightly re-sync notices what changed at the provider
scenarios.say: Someone renames one secret, deletes another and adds a third directly at the providers. Privilege is not told. When the lab clock crosses 02:00 the connected stores re-synchronise: metadata only, no value is ever requested.

steps.say: A secret is renamed in the AWS console.
Another is deleted at AWS.
A new secret appears in a GCP project.
The clock moves to 01:59: the nightly re-sync has not run.
One more minute: 02:00. The nightly re-sync runs.
